newsitem.title: USA: Houston ship channel still shut Thursday evening.
newsitem.headline: Houston ship channel still shut Thursday evening.

text.p: The Houston Ship Channel remained closed Thursday evening after the U.S. Coast Guard shut it following the capsizing of a barge carrying a pair of zinc bromide tanks and other materials earlier, a Coast Guard official said.
"The safety zone is still in effect," said Lieutenant Elizabeth Becker at the Marine Safety Office in Houston.
"We want to get the channel open as fast as we can, but we don't want it to be a hazard to navigation," she said, declining to estimate exactly when it would reopen.
She said officials continued to search the accident zone for two tanks containing potentially hazardous material.
"We're still continuing our search for the tanks," Becker said.

Earlier she said that while the barge had been towed away, the Army Corps of Engineers needed to close the accident area to search for the two 500-barrel tanks of zinc bromide that were aboard the barge.
She said the chemical did not appear to be a serious threat to aquatic life.
"The concern is a ship could hit the tanks. We want to make the sure the channel is free of the tanks," she said earlier.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
